# Five-rung closure

*Move down a short ladder: each rung either **passes** or tells you exactly what to
change next.*

## 1. Reproduce

Run the command or test the ticket names. Capture full output. If you cannot reproduce,
fix environment or invocation before touching product logic.

## 2. Minimise the surface

Open only the files the trace or ticket points to; read parallel independent slices; stop
when the faulty span is identified.

## 3. Patch once, coherently

One logical change set; no drive-by refactors. Match style. Respect implied invariants:
bounds, guards for shared state, monotonic timing when relevant, explicit boundary
comparisons.

## 4. Project proof

Re-run the **same** check class that failed. Read errors to the end. If it still fails,
change diagnosis — not punctuation — before a second full patch cycle.

## 5. Closure check

- Every task verb has a matching artefact on disk.
- Every artefact is where the grader can see it.
- Version control: identity set, explicit staging, one-line message when commits apply.

## Tool budget

Batch independent reads; serialize writes. If exploration stalls, descend the ladder anyway
with the smallest verifiable slice — partial proof beats endless intake.

## Notes

One verified line when you learned a durable quirk; skip diary noise.

## Exit

Ladder complete for the named defect — stop.
